passages.provision_quote: On and after January 1, 2025, an agency responsible for the development or operation of bikeways or highways where bicycle travel is permitted shall not install a new sharrow on a highway that has a posted speed limit greater than 30 miles per hour, except at or near an intersection for the purpose of connecting a Class I, Class II, or Class IV bikeway through the intersection.
passages.note: A design standard barring sharrows and Class III bikeways on faster roads and from Active Transportation Program eligibility; it sets no split between road capacity and other modes.

rows.reasoning: The only evidence is SB 1216 (2023-2024), which Blakespear authored; it bars new sharrows on highways posted above 30 miles per hour and bars the commission from adding Class III bikeway or sharrow projects to the Active Transportation Program. That is a bikeway design and safety standard inside an existing active-transportation program, so it does not say whether to invest in "pedestrian infrastructure, cycling networks, and public transit over new road capacity", to "invest equally", or to "focus on road capacity and traffic flow". No surviving passage speaks to the split the rungs order.
needs_source: A Blakespear record or first-person statement on the split between road capacity and transit/bike/pedestrian spending (for example a vote on a state transportation funding package that shifts money between highway capacity and transit)
